name: Swazi Sishwala
description: Sishwala, a stiff maize porridge, is Eswatini's most essential staple starch, eaten daily alongside relishes.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes until very thick and smooth.
steps: Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.

name: Swazi Sidvudvu
description: Sidvudvu, a pumpkin and cornmeal porridge, is a genuine Swazi comfort food - real pumpkin isn't a distinct item here, so winter squash stands in for a similar orange, sweet flesh.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Squash, winter, acorn, cooked, baked, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Squash, winter, acorn, cooked, baked, without salt

steps_detailed: Mash the squash smooth.
Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water with the mashed squash.
Cook, stirring often, 15-18 minutes until thick and smooth.
steps: Mash the squash smooth.

name: Swazi Emasi
description: Emasi, a thick, tangy fermented milk, is a genuine Swazi staple, traditionally eaten with sishwala - real emasi ferments naturally over several days, so this leans on real yogurt for a similarly thick, tangy dairy product.
steps_detailed: Serve the yogurt as-is, alongside sishwala or on its own.

name: Swazi Grilled Meat
description: Grilled meat, a beloved Swazi way of preparing beef for gatherings, echoing the wider Southern African braai tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the garlic and oil.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 12-15 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.

name: Swazi Chakalaka
description: Chakalaka, a spicy vegetable relish, is beloved across Eswatini as it is throughout Southern Africa.

name: Swazi Sitfubi
description: Sitfubi, a sour, fermented porridge drink, a genuine Swazi beverage - real sitfubi ferments over several days, so this quicker version approximates a milder version of the tang.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal with the vinegar and 2 cups water.
Let sit at room temperature 6-8 hours to develop a slight tang.
Strain and serve chilled.
